decision_authority.policy: MRX continuous quality-gated publication and two-image article creative directive

title: Existing Wells vs. Future Locations in a DCF Model
findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 2125a059867fe60a769f6d3f8852bc9605a1f9926d548855a6ec2189199403b7; all 7 declared official sources passed live access review.
Regulatory production, wellbore, permit, GIS, public-company disclosure, and commodity benchmark claims remain bounded to their official government sources and stated limitations.

The article uses no fabricated owners, wells, leases, production, forecasts, prices, costs, ownership decimals, reserves, transaction values, market evidence, testimonials, or owner-specific title, legal, tax, surveying, investment, reserve, engineering, or valuation conclusions.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Oil and Gas Production Data (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas publishes production compilations and summaries based on information reported to the Commission by operators and provides multiple production-query and download paths.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the page to identify a public regulatory production source and does not treat reported production as proof of title, a complete owner cash flow, a reserve report, a forecast, or market value.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Production Data Query System FAQs (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission explains that Texas oil production may be reported at the lease level, online production information has a reporting lag, and records can change as corrected, revised, or delinquent reports arrive.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses these limitations to bound production-history work and does not infer individual-well volumes, payment ownership, title, or future production from a regulatory record.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Wellbore Query (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission Wellbore Query accepts criteria including district, lease or gas-well identifier, county, field, operator, drilling-permit number, API number, current or historical status, and well type.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the query only to improve well, lease, permit, operator, field, and status identity; it does not treat a query result as proof of title, unit participation, production, reserves, future drilling, owner payment, or value.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Drilling Permit W-1 Query (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission Drilling Permit W-1 Query exposes searchable permit and status fields such as API number, county, operator, lease, field, filing purpose, well profile, approved date, and completion status.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses a permit as dated regulatory status evidence and explicitly does not infer guaranteed drilling, completion, commercial production, capital allocation, owner payment, timing, reserves, or value.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Public GIS Viewer (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission Public GIS Viewer provides map context for oil, gas, pipeline, survey, lease, and well information and warns that mapped boundaries can be approximate and are not authoritative legal, engineering, or surveying records.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses GIS only for location and regulatory context and does not infer title, exact boundaries, legal descriptions, surveying conclusions, development certainty, or owner-specific value from the map.

sources_inspected.label: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Oil and Gas Rules (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The SEC oil-and-gas rules guidance discusses public-company reserve definitions, development-plan evidence, technical support, and timing considerations for undeveloped locations.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article identifies that public-company disclosure context and does not use the guidance to classify a private owner’s acreage, create a reserve report, replace qualified engineering work, or establish owner-specific value.

sources_inspected.label: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Spot Prices for Crude Oil and Petroleum Products (accessed 2026-08-11)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The U.S. Energy Information Administration publishes dated crude-oil and petroleum-product spot-price series with definitions, source notes, and historical downloads.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses EIA spot prices only as dated benchmark context and does not treat a benchmark as the owner’s realized price, a future price forecast, or an owner-specific valuation conclusion.
